subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Soil Mechanics: What Lies Beneath
description: A micro-lesson that makes Soil Mechanics: What Lies Beneath usable.

hook.text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa tilts because one side of its foundation sits on softer clay.

buildup.text: Soil bearing capacity determines how much weight ground can support. Sand holds more than clay. Rock holds most.

discovery.text: Karl Terzaghi founded modern soil mechanics in 1925. He proved soil behaves like a material, not just dirt.

twist.text: Liquefaction turns solid ground into liquid during earthquakes. Sandy soil loses all bearing capacity in seconds.

climax.text: Before any building starts, geotechnical engineers drill boreholes and test soil samples. The foundation depends on it.

punchline.text: No building is stronger than the ground beneath it.

quiz.question: What is liquefaction in soil mechanics?
options: Water underground dissolving minerals and creating voids
Sandy soil losing all bearing capacity during an earthquake and acting like liquid
Heavy rain saturating clay until it can no longer support weight
